name: Return of Blue Lake to Taos Pueblo
summary: Congress restored 48,000 acres including Blue Lake to Taos Pueblo by H.R. 471 (Pub. L. 91-550, 84 Stat. 1437), signed Dec 15, 1970. Pueblo's account dates the taking to 1906. Tribe's own page and Nixon signing remarks agree on acreage and date.

name: Menominee restoration to reservation status
summary: BIA release of April 22, 1975 states about 200,000 acres of forest land and a sawmill returned to reservation status after termination (restoration statute 1973 [from-memory: Pub. L. 93-197]; BIA page read does not cite it).

name: Pe' Sla returned to the Oceti Sakowin
nation: Oceti Sakowin (Great Sioux Nation); led by Rosebud Sioux Tribe (role inferred from headlines)
location: Black Hills, South Dakota (Rapid City area)
summary: 1,942 acres purchased for $9 million and returned Nov 30, 2012; ILTF and its affiliate Indian Land Capital Company provided $900,000 fast financing; public fundraising through LastRealIndians and ILTF. 2025-26: Pe' Sla faces a mining drilling controversy per Lakota People's Law Project.

name: Tuluwat (Duluwat) Island returned to the Wiyot Tribe
summary: Oct 21, 2019: Eureka City Council voted unanimously and Mayor Susan Seaman and Wiyot Chair Ted Hernandez signed a deed returning about 200 acres without sale or lawsuit. Earlier: tribe bought 1.5 acres incl. the village site in 2000 (>$100,000 raised) and the city gave 40 acres in 2004. [V3] Source article gives both "200 acres" (lede) and "roughly 202 acres" (later passage) for the island; 200 retained as the rounded figure.

name: National Bison Range restored to CSKT
summary: Restoration approved in the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (Pub. L. 116-260, signed Dec 27, 2020; Montana Water Rights Protection Act). Sen. Daines' Jan 15, 2021 release says Interior Secretary Bernhardt signed the transfer papers and calls it an 18,800-acre refuge. DOI release dated June 23, 2021 (confirmed) says about 18,800.22 acres were transferred from USFWS to BIA to be held in trust for CSKT; it gives no separate signing date. Two-year management transition.

name: Adler Ranch (Little Sur River) returned to Esselen Tribe
summary: Western Rivers Conservancy moved to buy the 1,199-acre ranch, then the Esselen Tribe of Monterey County purchased it from the Conservancy using a $4.5M California Natural Resources Agency grant (WRC release dated July 27, 2020, says the sale was finalized 'on Friday', i.e. about July 24, 2020; day inferred). First ancestral land returned to the tribe.

name: Elliotsville Foundation returns 735 acres to Penobscot Nation
summary: Announced Oct 30, 2020 by Penobscot Nation and the Elliotsville Foundation; described as a land stewardship agreement. Whether fee title transferred or a stewardship instrument was used is not clear in the sources read.

name: Cheyenne River Youth Project buys land beside Bear Butte
location: Black Hills, adjoining Bear Butte (Mato Paha) State Park, South Dakota
summary: Nonprofit announced April 11, 2024 it bought nearly 40 acres next to Bear Butte for Lakota access; price not disclosed. Note: purchased by a Native-led nonprofit rather than tribal government.

name: Oneida Indian Nation reacquisition and trust applications
location: Madison and Oneida counties, New York
summary: Nation bought land within its 1794 grant after 1970s litigation; City of Sherrill v. Oneida Indian Nation, 544 U.S. 197 (2005) held reacquired land was taxable absent trust; 2013 agreement caps trust at 25,000 acres, about 18,000 acres in trust as of 2022 (Wikipedia). BIA fact sheet (Feb 2023) describes a decision for about 270 acres in 16 parcels. Acres are an estimate.

name: Blue Creek Salmon Sanctuary and Yurok Tribal Community Forest
location: Lower Klamath River, Del Norte and Humboldt counties, California
summary: Western Rivers Conservancy effort of 23 years; final phase of 14,968 acres transferred May 30, 2025; WRC acquired from Green Diamond Resource Company 2009-2017. Total cost reported $56M, of which $8M public grants. California's largest tribal land return. HCN rounds to 47,100 acres / 14,000 acres.

name: 'O Rew Redwoods Gateway returned to Yurok Tribe
summary: Yurok Tribe home page: July 28, 2026 announcement that Save the Redwoods League transferred 125 acres; public gateway opens Aug 1, 2026.

name: Tule River Tribe reclaims 17,030 acres in Yowlumne Hills
location: Sierra Nevada foothills and Central Valley, California
summary: Announced Oct 29, 2025 with tule elk reintroduction; funded by CNRA Tribal Nature-Based Solutions, WCB Habitat Conservation Fund and private philanthropy; Conservation Fund facilitated. Seller not identified.

name: Southern Sierra Miwuk Nation regains land bordering Yosemite
location: Adjacent to Yosemite National Park, California
summary: Pacific Forest Trust release (Dec 2-3, 2025): nearly 900 acres stewarded by the trust for 20 years return to the Nation after 175 years. Mechanism not stated.

name: WélmeltiɁ Preserve returned to Washoe Tribe
location: Northern Sierra Nevada, northeast of Lake Tahoe (formerly Loyalton Ranch), California
summary: Tribe announced the completed purchase (Native News Online byline Feb 10, 2026; article says 'announced Wednesday', so likely Feb 11; no completion date given). 10,274 acres, formerly Loyalton Ranch, northeast of Lake Tahoe about 20 miles north of Reno (state not stated); held by the tribe's Waší·šiw Land Trust (established 2025); partners Northern Sierra Partnership, Feather River Land Trust, California WCB. Price not disclosed. Article calls it the largest tribal land return ever completed in the Sierra Nevada and the third largest in California.

name: Mechoopda regain 450 acres in Big Chico Creek watershed
summary: CNRA release: two properties beside Big Chico Creek Ecological Reserve funded through the Tribal Nature-Based Solutions Program; sellers unnamed. Date inferred as June 2026 from news listing.

name: Blues Beach transfer to Kai Poma (Pomo tribes)
nation: Sherwood Valley Band of Pomo; Round Valley Indian Tribes; Coyote Valley Band of Pomo
summary: California Transportation Commission approved on June 26, 2026; state land managed by Caltrans; deed not recorded as of early July 2026 reporting. Enabling legislation reported as SB 231 (2021) by an opinion site (Legal Insurrection); not independently confirmed. Reported deed terms bar commercial activity and require public access (single opinion source).

name: Mi'kmaq Nation Bridgewater parcel
summary: Maine Public (June 26, 2026): the parcel is 'over 3,400 acres' in the lede but 'nearly 3,400 acres' in a photo caption (article inconsistent). The Conservation Fund bought it in 2025 from a local forester and held it for the tribe; $1.9M is the amount still to be raised to complete the purchase, not stated as the total price. Sixth of 11 Tributary Land Returns projects; 'more than double' the tribe's holdings (no before/after acreage given).

name: Houlton Band of Maliseet acquires land near Wilderness Pines
summary: 1,327 acres acquired the year before July 2026, per Bangor Daily News; single source.

name: Tributary Land Returns (Wabanaki, Maine)
nation: Houlton Band of Maliseet; Mi'kmaq Nation; Passamaquoddy (Motahkomikuk, Sipayik); Penobscot
summary: Eight-year, $50M effort to return 50,000 acres in 11 parcels; six completed and 'about halfway' as of July 2026 (Bangor Daily News, July 6, 2026). Remaining parcels named: Kennebec River mouth; Passamaquoddy forest on the south branch of the Penobscot; 30,000+ acres for the Penobscot Nation near Katahdin Woods and Waters; a Passamaquoddy portion along the Cobscook-Machias canoe route. Partners: five Wabanaki tribes, the Wabanaki Commission on Land and Stewardship, and First Light, whose members include TNC Maine, Trust for Public Land, Maine Coast Heritage Trust, Appalachian Mountain Club, Forest Society of Maine and The Conservation Fund. Start year not stated (about 2018 only by arithmetic from 'eight-year').

name: Monument Mountain (Peeskawso Peak) parcel to Stockbridge-Munsee
location: Great Barrington / Stockbridge area, Berkshire County, Massachusetts
summary: Tribal Business News (Apr 30, 2025): purchase of 372 acres on Monument Mountain finalized at $2.5M (asking price $3M), mainly a $2.26M state grant awarded in 2023; land first listed 2022. The Berkshire Edge article that gives 351 acres is dated Aug 30, 2023 (grant announcement; its caption says $2.6M while its body says $2.26M); the 351-to-372 difference is unexplained, so 372 is the closing-report figure and 351 the earlier one.

name: Six Nations Iroquois Cultural Center buys Adirondack land
summary: Native News Online (Mar 17, 2026): over 600 acres bought from Paul Smith's College for $1.1M with TNC funding; earlier 330-acre parcel from Adirondack Land Trust in 2022. Article's '900-acre' total conflicts with 600 + 330. Purchase by a cultural center nonprofit.

name: Siletz Rocky Shores parcel near Yachats
summary: Nearly seven acres, $120,000 appraised price (View the Future gave $55,000; McKenzie River Trust brokered). Sale not confirmed closed as of Oct 13, 2026 update. Access by invitation only.

name: Heron's Nest returned to the Duwamish Tribe
location: West Seattle ridge near industrial district, Washington
summary: Buffalo's Fire (Aug 6, 2026): 3.56 acres turned over June 13 (year inferred 2026), in partnership with Shared Spaces Foundation; legal mechanism not stated.

name: Pamunkey 13-acre return (headline only)
summary: Washington Post headline (July 28, 2026) refers to 13 acres for cultural and educational purposes; article blocked to automated reading. Do not publish details until verified.

name: White Horse Hill returned to Spirit Lake Nation
summary: HCN (Feb 2026) reports 680 acres of White Horse Hill National Game Preserve within the reservation's original boundaries returned from USFWS; date and statute not given.

name: NANA Regional Corporation land transfers (Alaska)
summary: HCN (Feb 2026) reports nearly 28,000 acres transferred to NANA under ANCSA; ANCSA conveyed up to 44 million acres to for-profit regional and village corporations. ALASKA IS A DISTINCT LEGAL CONTEXT. Transfer date not stated.

name: Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (ANCSA)
summary: Pub. L. 92-203, signed Dec 18, 1971: up to 44 million acres and about $962.5M to 12 land-owning regional corporations and 200+ village corporations. Not a treaty and not a tribal land return; criticized by some Alaska Natives. DISTINCT LEGAL CONTEXT.

name: Land Buy-Back Program for Tribal Nations
summary: DOI: nearly 3 million acres restored to tribal trust; about $1.69B paid to individual owners; appropriations ended Nov 2022; conclusion announced Dec 4, 2023. A consolidation of fractionated interests, not recovery of ceded land.

name: California Tribal Nature-Based Solutions land return program
summary: CNRA says the program has returned 40,574.94 acres statewide and invested $100M+ (figure from the Mechoopda release; undated).

name: Fort Reno return campaign (Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes)
summary: About 6,700 acres held by USDA (Oklahoma and Central Plains Agricultural Research Center); the tribes say it should have reverted in 1948. As of March 2026 the House Agriculture Committee advanced H.R. 7567 (34-17) which would remove the sunset on the bar against USDA disposing of Fort Reno. Sources cite other figures (about 6,900 acres 1949 bill; a 10,000-acre discrepancy cited by Gov. Reggie Wassana).

name: Menominee Legend Lake buybacks (Wisconsin Supreme Court)
summary: WPR (June 29, 2026): Wisconsin Supreme Court ruled 4-3 that Legend Lake Property Owners Association cannot sue to block the tribe's buybacks (tribal sovereign immunity). WPR says 40 parcels; a law professor says 40 acres; unit unclear.

name: Black Hills (He Sapa) claim and LANDBACK Mount Rushmore campaign
summary: United States v. Sioux Nation of Indians, 448 U.S. 371 (1980), held the Act of Feb 28, 1877 effected a taking requiring just compensation (5% interest on a $17.1M principal from 1877); the Sioux have refused the money (AP: about $105M) because the land was never for sale. NDN Collective's LANDBACK campaign (launched 2020) seeks closure of Mount Rushmore and return of public lands in the Black Hills. Acreage not stated in sources read.

name: Puyallup Tribe Land Claims Settlement
summary: Puyallup Tribe of Indians Settlement Act of 1989; Wikipedia gives about $162-163M including the Port of Tacoma. Acreage not stated in the source.

name: Santa Ynez Chumash Camp 4 trust land
summary: Wikipedia says 1,390 acres placed in trust; its own date is inconsistent (2017 vs 2019). Litigation not described. Treat as unverified.

name: Sogorea Te' Land Trust land returns and Shuumi Land Tax
summary: Named sites include Lisjan (East Oakland), 'Ookwe (Richmond), Rammay (West Oakland), West Berkeley Shellmound. Acreage not published on the pages read. Start year approximate [from-memory]; ProPublica exempt 2019.

name: Native Land Conservancy land holdings
nation: Wampanoag and other southern New England Native communities
location: Massachusetts (11 towns) and Madeline Island, Wisconsin
summary: Holdings page: 'more than 295 acres across 11 towns in Massachusetts' plus 8.5 acres on Madeline Island, WI (sum 303.5). 18 named holdings; tribal affiliation per holding not stated.

name: Real Rent Duwamish
summary: Voluntary rent paid by Seattle residents; 100% to Duwamish Tribal Services. Start date not on the page read. Not a land return itself.

name: Hawaiian Home Lands (Hawaii, distinct legal context)
summary: DHHL administers about 203,981 acres of trust lands under the 1920 Hawaiian Homes Commission Act; 47,086 lease applications by 29,451 beneficiaries. State program, not a US treaty or tribal land. HAWAII DISTINCT LEGAL CONTEXT.

name: Right Relationship Boulder Land Group
summary: Ally-led group acting at tribes' request; funds tribal youth camps, seeks plant-gathering access and tribal guidance at Fort Chambers. No land return described on the page.

name: Miccosukee Tribe land expansion bill (headline only)
nation: Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida
summary: NILL headline list: Native News Online 1/2/2026 'Trump veto stalls effort to expand Miccosukee Tribal lands' and Grist 1/9/2026. Articles not read.

name: Ute Indian Tribe and Utah trust land transfers (headline only)
summary: Salt Lake Tribune 7/29/2026 headline on a quiet effort that undercut the tribe's land back hopes. Article not read.

name: California pledge to open 7% of lands and waters to tribes (headline only)
summary: LA Times headline of March 17, 2026; article blocked to automated reading. Do not cite specifics.
